scope: Corollary 1.2 (Eisenbud–Green–Harris and lex-plus-powers in characteristic zero) of the manuscript “The Artinian Lex-Plus-Powers Betti Theorem” (preprints/The-Artinian-Lex-Plus-Powers-Betti-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 200 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 81874e1994ff2773), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let F be a field of characteristic zero, let SF = F[x1, . . . , xn], 1 ≤ c ≤ n, 2 ≤ a1 ≤ · · · ≤ ac, PF = (xa1 1 , . . . , xac c ), with the standard grading and lexicographic order x1 > · · · > xn. Suppose that a homogeneous ideal I ⊆ SF contains a homogeneous regular sequence f1, . . . , fc with deg fi = ai. For d ≥ 0, put qd = dimF Id − dimF (PF )d. This integer lies between zero and the number of degree-d monomials outside PF . Let Jd be the sum of (PF )d and the span of the qd lexicographically greatest such monomials. Then J = L d≥0 Jd is a homogeneous ideal, and for this single ideal dimF (SF /I)d = dimF (SF /J)d (d ≥ 0), βSF p,j (SF /I) ≤ βSF p,j (SF /J) (p ≥ 0, j ∈ Z). There is no restriction on the degrees or number of the additional generators of I.
